skill.description: Analyze YouTube comments and replies through SocialDataX to identify audience themes, pain points, buying concerns, unmet needs, and actionable recommendations.

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives involving Markdown backticks, documented service links, legitimate API configuration, or readable Chinese text. A separate medium-severity concern is automatic execution of an unpinned npm package with access to the configured API credential. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or concealed payloads in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The CLI examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest automatically with npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and use a lockfile with integrity verification where possible. Request installation approval and isolate execution from unrelated credentials.

content.user_title: Analyze YouTube Comments for Audience Insights
content.value_statement: YouTube comment threads can make recurring audience needs difficult to identify. This skill organizes retrieved comments and replies into evidence-based themes, questions, and practical recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve YouTube video comments through the SocialDataX CLI or available MCP tools.
Retrieve replies using reply tokens returned with top-level comments.
Expand retrieval with pagination tokens, page counts, and item limits.
Request top-level comments sorted by popularity or descending time.
Organize visible feedback into themes, pain points, purchase concerns, unmet needs, and FAQ candidates.
Separate quoted evidence from interpretation and report sample coverage or partial retrieval.
limitations: Live retrieval requires a SocialDataX API key, network access, and sufficient service balance.
Direct CLI use requires Node.js and npm; external package implementation is not included in the skill.
Findings describe retrieved comments and replies, not all YouTube users or platform-wide opinion.
The workflow is read-only and does not log in, publish replies, like content, or modify accounts.

use_cases.title: Plan Follow-Up Videos
use_cases.description: Identify recurring audience questions and turn supported themes into follow-up video topics.

use_cases.title: Research Product Pain Points
use_cases.description: Review comments on product videos to distinguish reported problems, unmet needs, and purchase concerns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Customer FAQ
use_cases.description: Convert recurring questions and reply discussions into FAQ candidates with visible supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize One Comment Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the first page of comments for [YouTube video URL]. List main themes, quote visible evidence, and state the sample limits.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Questions and Concerns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review up to 100 comments for [YouTube video URL]. Group recurring questions and purchase concerns, separate evidence from interpretation, and suggest FAQ topics.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Reply Discussions
prompt_templates.prompt: For [YouTube video URL], retrieve one comment page and inspect replies to three relevant threads. Report disagreements, unresolved questions, and coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bounded Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: For [YouTube video URL], retrieve at most three pages and 200 comments. Produce an evidence-based needs brief. Preserve partial results and explain coverage gaps.

output_examples.input: Illustrative sample: viewers ask for a slower setup walkthrough and say the cable connection is unclear.
output: Theme: setup instructions need more detail.
Evidence: the supplied sample requests slower pacing and clearer cable guidance.
Action: create a focused setup walkthrough.
Coverage: this illustrative sample does not establish audience-wide frequency.

output_examples.input: Illustrative sample: comments ask about subscription pricing, and a reply asks whether a free plan exists.
output: Purchase concern: uncertainty about ongoing cost.
FAQ candidate: What plans are available, and is there a free option?
Action: verify current pricing before drafting an answer.
Boundary: these comments do not establish the actual pricing or plan availability.

best_practices: Start with one page and set explicit page or item limits before expanding retrieval.
Quote only returned comments and distinguish visible evidence from interpretation.
Use a reviewed, pinned CLI version and keep the API key outside prompts and shared reports.
anti_patterns: Treating a first-page sample as representative of every viewer or the whole platform.
Using unrestricted retrieval without considering service balance, request volume, or task scope.
Inventing customer quotes or presenting inferred needs as verified facts.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a YouTube video URL and the research question you want to investigate.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Configure SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY and ensure service balance. Direct CLI use needs Node.js and npm; available MCP tools provide another retrieval route.

faq.question: Can it retrieve replies?
faq.answer: Yes. Reply retrieval uses reply_token values returned with top-level comments.

faq.question: Does it cover every comment?
faq.answer: Not by default. The workflow starts with one page and reports the retrieved sample and any coverage gaps.

faq.question: Can it post comments or change my account?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow retrieves comments and replies without login, posting, likes, or account modification.

faq.question: What happens when retrieval fails?
faq.answer: Preserve partial results and resume from a valid continuation token when available. Balance errors require resolving funding rather than repeated retries.
